newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-BARRANGER TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN SARAZEN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BARRANGER TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN SARAZEN OPEN.

text.p: Todd Barranger upstaged his better-known rivals to grab the first-round lead at the $1.9 million Sarazen World Open on Thursday.

Barranger, who qualified for the unique event by winning this year's Thailand Open, compiled five birdies and an eagle for a seven-under-par 65 in beautiful weather at Chateau Elan in the rolling Georgia countryside outside Atlanta.
He led by one stroke from defending champion Frank Nobilo, while a star-studded bunch at 68 comprised Americans Fred Couples, Craig Stadler, John Cook and Scott Hoch, and Zimbabwean Nick Price.
Barranger, 28, made a shaky start when he hooked his drive into trees at his first hole, but he sank a 20-footer to save par and never looked back.
Although he lives not far from here in Knoxville, Tennessee, Barranger played primarily on the Asian Tour this year after recovering from testicular cancer.
He played the PGA Tour in 1994 but lost his card, before being diagnosed with cancer in February last year. He took nearly the rest of the year off to fight the disease.
"It wasn't until June this year that my strength started to return so that I could play consecutive weeks," he explained.
"I used to lift weights, but my body won't allow me to now. My muscles won't recover."
Kiwi Nobilo, meanwhile, enjoyed playing with Jack Nicklaus for what he believes was the first time in competition.
Before they teed off, tournament host Gene Sarazen hit a ceremonial tee shot and wished them well.

"He (Sarazen) is one of the greatest players that ever lived. When he wishes you well and you tee it up with the greatest golfer off all time (Nicklaus), it's pretty hard not to get nervous," Nobilo explained. "I was extremely happy to play as well as I did."
The event is restricted to national open winners the past two years, as well as major champions and a handful of selections by Sarazen.
Couples fell into the last category. At the Masters in April, he received a personal request from Sarazen, which he could hardly turn down.
"If he hadn't asked me, I wouldn't have played," Couples admitted.
